requirementIndex.title: WHEN `vite.config.ts` is evaluated during a build or dev server start THE SYSTEM SHALL add a `__BUILD_TIME__: JSON.stringify(Date.now())` entry to the existing `define` block, alongside the existing `__APP_VERSION__` entry.
WHEN the `define` block is written THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the existing `__APP_VERSION__: JSON.stringify(pkg.version)` entry unmodified.
WHEN `Date.now()` is passed through `JSON.stringify` THE SYSTEM SHALL produce an unquoted numeric literal so that `__BUILD_TIME__` is injected as a `number`, not a `string`.
THE SYSTEM SHALL capture the timestamp exactly once per build/config evaluation, with no runtime clock reads, no `setInterval`, and no re-render-on-tick behavior anywhere in the feature.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT compute or display a "time since build" relative counter.
WHEN `src/vite-env.d.ts` is updated THE SYSTEM SHALL add a `declare const __BUILD_TIME__: number` line alongside the existing `__APP_VERSION__` declaration.
WHEN the new declaration is added THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the existing `declare const __APP_VERSION__: string` line unmodified.
WHEN `HeaderBuildBadge` renders THE SYSTEM SHALL read the injected `__BUILD_TIME__` global and construct a `Date` from it.
WHEN formatting the build date THE SYSTEM SHALL call `toLocaleString` with no explicit locale argument (`undefined`), so THE SYSTEM SHALL render the timestamp using the viewer's browser locale.
WHEN formatting the build date THE SYSTEM SHALL call `toLocaleString` with no explicit `timeZone` option, so THE SYSTEM SHALL render the timestamp in the viewer's local timezone.
WHEN formatting the build date THE SYSTEM SHALL use `{ dateStyle: 'medium', timeStyle: 'short' }` as the formatting options.
WHEN the badge renders text content THE SYSTEM SHALL render exactly `built {formatted}`, with no other label variants.
THE SYSTEM SHALL implement `HeaderBuildBadge` as a component that accepts no props and holds no internal state.
THE SYSTEM SHALL locate the component exclusively at `src/components/header-build-badge/header-build-badge.tsx`.

WHEN the badge renders THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the same pill treatment as `FooterVersionBadge`: `rounded-full`, `border border-[var(--border)]`, `bg-[var(--code-bg)]`, `px-2 py-0.5`, `text-xs`, `text-[var(--text)]`.
THE SYSTEM SHALL consume the existing hand-rolled CSS custom properties (`--border`, `--code-bg`, `--text`) via Tailwind arbitrary-value syntax, the same mechanism `FooterVersionBadge` uses.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT add `--background`, `--foreground`, `--muted-foreground`, or any `@theme` block to `src/index.css` or `tailwind.config.ts`.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT introduce any Shadcn semantic token migration as part of this feature.
WHERE styling decisions are needed THE SYSTEM SHALL reuse `FooterVersionBadge`'s approach read-only, without modifying any file under `src/components/footer-version-badge/`.
WHEN the badge is positioned THE SYSTEM SHALL apply `fixed right-3 top-3` to the outer wrapper, placing it in the top-right corner of the viewport.
THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the badge's fixed position distinct from `FooterVersionBadge`'s fixed `right-3 bottom-3` position, so the two badges never overlap.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT set an explicit `z-index` on the badge, since its top-right position does not overlap the bottom-right footer badge.
WHEN the page is printed THE SYSTEM SHALL apply `print:hidden` to the badge's outer wrapper so the badge does not appear in print output.
THE SYSTEM SHALL render the badge as purely presentational markup, with no `onClick` handler, no `<a>`/`<Link>` element, and no clipboard API usage.
THE SYSTEM SHALL render the timestamp as a plain visible text node with no `aria-hidden` attribute, so it remains reachable by screen readers like any other static text.
WHEN the app runs in dev, staging, or production THE SYSTEM SHALL render the same badge markup unconditionally, with no `import.meta.env.DEV`/`PROD` gating.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT expose any props on `HeaderBuildBadge`, and SHALL NOT add any new settings, context, or store entry to configure the badge.
WHEN `src/App.tsx` is updated THE SYSTEM SHALL mount `<HeaderBuildBadge />` once, alongside the existing `<FooterVersionBadge />` mount.
WHEN the mount is added THE SYSTEM SHALL make no other markup changes to `src/App.tsx`.
THE SYSTEM SHALL ensure no file other than `src/App.tsx` mounts `HeaderBuildBadge`.
WHEN any view of the (currently single-page) app renders THE SYSTEM SHALL display the badge, since it is mounted at the app root.
THE SYSTEM SHALL treat `src/components/header-build-badge/` as exclusively owned by this feature, adding nothing unrelated to that directory.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT add files or feature-specific logic outside `src/components/header-build-badge/` other than the integration touches to `src/vite-env.d.ts`, `vite.config.ts`, and `src/App.tsx`.
THE SYSTEM SHALL implement the feature using only `react` (already a dependency) and native `Intl`/`Date`/`toLocaleString` APIs and Tailwind utility classes.
THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT add any new npm package to satisfy this feature's requirements.
